classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied construction scaffold, measure perpendicular heights, identify each height and baseline as opposite and adjacent, and divide the corresponding measurements. These are routine linked construction, measurement and ratio procedures; no independent similarity proof or trigonometric insight is requested.

content.prompt: Use your protractor to draw an angle of $31^{\circ}$. Mark off distances of $4\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$. Draw a perpendicular at each point. Measure the heights and find, approximately, the ratio $\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$ in each triangle.

spec.description: Four nested right triangles share the 31-degree left vertex. Vertical perpendiculars meet the rising ray at horizontal distances 4, 5, 7 and 10 cm. The baseline and ray extend beyond the largest triangle. Stacked dimension arrows run from the common vertex, ordered 10, 7, 5 and 4 cm from top to bottom. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular heights are proportional to the horizontal distances because the triangles share their acute angles.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible; no measured heights or calculated ratios are supplied.

answer.worked:
The measured heights should be approximately $2.4\text{ cm}$, $3.0\text{ cm}$, $4.2\text{ cm}$ and $6.0\text{ cm}$, respectively.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{h_1}{4}&\approx\frac{2.4}{4}=0.60\\\frac{h_2}{5}&\approx\frac{3.0}{5}=0.60\\\frac{h_3}{7}&\approx\frac{4.2}{7}=0.60\\\frac{h_4}{10}&\approx\frac{6.0}{10}=0.60\end{align*}$$

Small measurement differences are expected. The ratios are approximately equal because the right-angled triangles are similar.
